newsitem.title: DUBAI: Fujairah oil storage seen boosting India trade.
newsitem.headline: Fujairah oil storage seen boosting India trade.

text.p: A planned 3.05 million barrel capacity oil product storage facility in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates will boost oil trading to the growing Indian subcontinent market, Gulf oil industry sources said on Monday.

A UAE-Dutch joint venture, involving state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) and Koninklijke van Ommeren NV, aims to offer an independent storage and product blending facility at Fujairah in 1998, the sources said.

"The plant will allow companies to store the whole range of products...The project is aiming for India and Pakistan...Facilities will be available for rent as in Rotterdam," said a UAE-based manager close to the project.
India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal are already important and regular refined product buyers from the Gulf and Singapore spot markets, and demand is set to grow strongly.
Other backers behind the Fujairah storage project are Swiss trading firm Vitol, Kuwait-based traders IPG and the Fujairah government, industry sources said.
Both Vitol and IPG are already involved in supplying refined products and crude to the Indian subcontinent, in particular to India Oil Corp (IOC) product tenders.
Traders and refiners with access to Fujairah storage would put them in a strong supply and pricing position.
The $75 million storage and product blending site will consist of 18 main tanks with 465,000 cubic metres of storage.
International companies have until October 22 to submit their offers to carry out construction of the plant.
A contract award will be made within two months, an industry source said.
